subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should gateway startup keep failing closed on required SecretRef failures, add a bounded generic retry/degrade policy, or expose configurable retry/circuit-breaker behavior for exec-backed secret providers?
rationale: The current behavior is source-reproducible and security-sensitive, but changing startup fail-fast semantics or adding `secrets.retryPolicy` would alter operator expectations, credential-provider side effects, and config surface.

options.title: Bounded generic startup policy
options.body: Add a core-owned, vendor-neutral startup retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy with clear logs and docs, without adding a broad user-facing retry config by default.

options.title: Configurable retry policy
options.body: Add an explicit `secrets.retryPolicy` surface and tests, accepting new config/API compatibility obligations.

options.title: External resolver guidance only
options.body: Keep core fail-fast behavior and direct users to batchable/cached resolvers or plugins, which avoids core policy churn but leaves supervisor restart storms as operator-managed risk.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic startup policy
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned, vendor-neutral startup retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy with clear logs and docs, without adding a broad user-facing retry config by default.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history connection to the SecretRef resolver and eager runtime snapshot behavior that the policy would change.
